inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 Annual Report adjusted-EBITDA reconciliation, 'Share-based compensation expense' 163 (FY2024 37, FY2023 -14 recovery). Nutrien's PSUs/RSUs/DSUs/SARs are CASH-settled (Note 7); only stock options settle in shares. EquityAwardTaxes nil. Expense is marked to the share price, so the 5-yr average (~0.35% of revenue) is used forward rather than the FY2025 spike.
inputs.share_count_basis: Q2 2026 weighted-average diluted shares 479.824m (NTR_Quarterly_Q2-2026 line 59). Held FLAT: SBC is expensed in the flows (and is mostly cash-settled anyway). Nutrien is an active repurchaser (FY2025 $551m; H1 2026 $320m; Q3 2026 pace ~$75-82m/month), so the flat count is funded, not a convention.
inputs.fx_note: Statements in USD (IFRS); NYSE quote in USD. TSX line quotes CAD and is not used.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD rate. Cost of equity: US 10y ~4.2% + beta ~0.85-0.9 x 5.0% ERP = ~8.6%. Cost of debt ~5.5% pre-tax (BBB senior notes) = ~4.1% after 25% tax. Weights ~76/24 equity/debt at market (mkt cap ~$33.6bn, drawn debt ~$11.4bn ex leases). WACC ~7.6%, rounded UP to 8.0% only for USD BBB credit spread drift -- NOT a cyclicality premium. Cyclicality is charged once, in the flows, via a mid-cycle margin path and a 25% bear weight with a potash-trough path. Same WACC in every scenario.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), leases as operating cost: lease cash (FY2025 principal $419m + lease interest ~$50-55m = ~$470m, 1.75% of revenue) deducted via lease_cost_pct_path; lease liabilities ($1,340m at 30-Jun-2026) EXCLUDED from net debt; D&A path is ex right-of-use depreciation (~$400m) so the lease is not charged twice in cash-tax EBIT.
inputs.nci_treatment: NCI is immaterial ($36m equity, ~$30m/yr profit). Flows are consolidated; NCI stock deducted once in the equity bridge.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF with the cyclical/non-US adaptations (SKILL.md routing row 2: cyclical operating company). Nutrien is an operating business (fertilizer production + ag retail), not a financial/REIT/holdco, so FCF is the right stream. First valuation of NTR (no memory entry, no prior DCF). CYCLICALITY: the FY0 revenue anchor is FY2025 continuing operations (FY2018's $3.6bn discontinued gain from the SQM/APC/ICL stake sales is excluded from every series and does not enter the build). EBITDA margin is anchored to Nutrien's own Adjusted EBITDA (FY2025 $6,046m = 22.5%; FY2024 $5,355m = 20.6%; FY2023 20.9%; FY2022 peak 32.1%; FY2020 trough 17.5%), NOT the CSV's cash-flow-derived EBITDA, and is taken ~0.6pp below the reported-adjusted figure to cover the recurring cash items Nutrien excludes from Adjusted EBITDA (restructuring, integration, cash-settled award payouts). The FY2022 Ukraine-war peak (EBITDA $12.2bn, FCF $5.6bn) is NOT used as an anchor; base mid-cycle margin 21.5% sits near the 2020-2025 median (21.7%) and below the 6-yr mean (23.2%, peak-inflated). FY2026 (year 1, ~75% elapsed at valuation date): H1 2026 sales $16.9bn (+8.5% y/y), H1 adj EBITDA $3.54bn (+6%), Retail guide $1.75-1.95bn, capex guide lowered to $1.95-2.05bn, D&A guide $2.4-2.5bn (incl ROU), effective tax on adjusted earnings 24-26%. CAPEX: elevated 2022-2024 ($2.5-2.6bn) included the potash ramp-up program, since slowed; forward capex held at ~7.0% of revenue (~= D&A ex-ROU) so the terminal year funds its own maintenance; no growth-capex holiday is assumed. WORKING CAPITAL: Retail is receivables/inventory heavy; 2020-2025 the cash gap between adjusted EBITDA and OCF+interest+tax averaged -$650m/yr on revenue growth of ~$6.8bn -- wc_capture set at -25% of the revenue change. INTEREST INCOME not stripped: Nutrien is net debt, not net cash. TIMING: net debt is the 30-Jun-2026 balance sheet (seasonally above the Dec-2025 $10.0bn because H1 builds Retail receivables) while FY2026 is projected in full; the H1 FCF already received and the seasonal working-capital build roughly offset, so no stub adjustment is made. Equity-accounted and other investments ($137m) added in the bridge at book.
inputs.last_fcf_note: last_fcf = reported FCF (OCF 4,007 - capex 2,005 = 2,002) - SBC 163 - interest income 0 = 1,839 per the house formula. Because Nutrien's awards are cash-settled, OCF already carries the payouts, so this deduction is conservative; further deducting lease principal 419 gives 1,420 on the treatment-(B) basis. It is a levered figure (after ~$738m cash interest) -- the engine's projections are unlevered and are not comparable to it directly.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5-yr CAGR (2.5%) diverges >30% from revenue (5.2%) and EPS (41.9%). All endpoint CAGRs are cycle artefacts: the 3-yr window starts at the FY2022 fertilizer peak (hence -11% revenue, -31% EPS/FCF), the 5-yr window at the FY2020 trough (hence +42% EPS). Equity is depressed by ~$9bn of buybacks 2018-2025. Forward growth is set from volumes + mid-cycle price, not from any CAGR.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series = reported FCF - SBC (equity-award taxes nil, interest income not stripped as net debt). Owner-FCF 5-yr CAGR 1.5% vs reported 2.5%: SBC rose from $69m to $163m, but it is cash-settled and mark-to-market, so this is share-price noise rather than growing stock dilution. FY2018 is continuing-ops only for revenue; reported FY2018 net income $3,573m includes $3,604m discontinued gain (continuing -$31m).

base.growth_rationale: FY2026 +7% tracks H1 +8.5% with a softer H2; FY2027 +2% as Belarus/BHP Jansen supply begins to weigh on potash price; thereafter ~3% (1-2% volume + inflation).
base.ebitda_margin_rationale: FY2026 ~22.2% (guidance-consistent adj EBITDA ~$6.5bn less ~0.6pp recurring excluded cash items) fading to a 21.5% mid-cycle.

scenario_narratives.base: Fertilizer markets normalise to mid-cycle. FY2026 lands near guidance (record potash volumes 14.2-14.8Mt, Retail adj EBITDA $1.75-1.95bn, capex ~$2.0bn). From 2027 BHP Jansen Stage 1 and a partial reopening of US access for Belarusian potash take the edge off potash pricing, but Canpotex discipline and trend demand growth in Asia/LatAm keep potash near mid-cycle. Nitrogen earns its North American gas-cost advantage; Phosphate is sold or shrunk with little value either way. Retail grows with crop inputs and proprietary-mix gains, and the ~$200m cost programme offsets inflation rather than lifting margins. Group EBITDA margin settles at 21.5% (2020-2025 median), capex ~= maintenance-level D&A.
scenario_narratives.bull: The 'structural FCF growth' story works. Potash stays tight through the decade as demand replenishes soils after record crops, Belarus remains sanctioned/contracted-out and Jansen ramps slowly into a growing market; automation (49% of ore tonnes in 2025) keeps controllable cash costs below $60/t. Retail proprietary products keep climbing past 32% of gross margin, the $200m savings drop through, Phosphate/Trinidad/Brazil Retail exits lift the mix, and capex settles at the low end of guidance. EBITDA margin reaches 24% -- below the 2021-22 boom (25.7-32.1%), so this is a strong mid-cycle, not a repeat of the peak.
scenario_narratives.bear: A potash down-cycle arrives in 2027-28: the US-Belarus deal admits sub-benchmark tonnes into Nutrien's home market while Jansen adds ~4Mt of lowest-cost Canadian supply, breaking Canpotex pricing discipline. Nitrogen margins compress on a US gas spike or cheap Middle East/Russian urea, and Retail suffers a farm-income squeeze (low grain prices, elevated >90-day receivables, goodwill impairment risk on the $7.0bn Retail NA CGU). Revenue falls ~9% over 2027-28 and EBITDA margin troughs at 18% (FY2020 trough was 17.5%) before recovering only to 19% -- i.e. the post-Jansen world is permanently less profitable than 2020-2025.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25%: there are two concrete, dated supply threats (BHP Jansen ramp from ~2027; the announced US-Belarus potash talks, Sept 2026) and the business is a commodity price-taker. Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it needs several independent things to go right at once (potash tightness persisting through Jansen, Belarus staying out, retail margin gains and the portfolio exits). Base 50%: mid-cycle is the single most likely state; the balance sheet (BBB, ~1.8x adj net debt/EBITDA) carries no solvency risk, so the bear is a margin case not a going-concern case.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Cyclical commodity producer bolted to a steadier, working-capital-heavy retail distributor. Value it on a mid-cycle owner-FCF path, never on the FY2022 peak, with cyclicality priced once in the flows (25/50/25 weights, a trough bear) and a single USD WACC. Leases are treated as an operating cost; the terminal value is capped at 14x unlevered FCF (cyclical cap), which binds in every scenario -- the market has historically paid ~7-8x EV/adj EBITDA, roughly 18x this FCF definition, so the gap between the cap and Gordon is the price of a re-rating thesis.
key_risks_to_valuation: Potash price: Jansen ramp (2027+) and Belarusian tonnes re-entering the US market
Nitrogen margin depends on the US natural-gas spread versus global marginal producers
Retail credit and the $7.0bn Retail North America goodwill (critical audit matter)
Working capital: Retail receivables/inventory absorb cash when revenue grows; the -25% capture is an estimate from a noisy 2020-2025 history
Year 1 (FY2026) is mostly elapsed; H2 seasonality is the swing factor for the June net-debt anchor
